items.title: Joe Muranyi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: Bunk used to call that whole band, Jim Robinson and George Lewis and [Lawrence] Marrero and what’s the name of the piano player, [Alton] Pernell, his wartime emergency band.

ctx.x: Well they were probably thrown together with him because he had so much hype going on, rediscovered, you know, working in the fields, and they got new teeth and all.

Well Bunk was a marvelous musician. Bunk used to call that whole band, Jim Robinson and George Lewis and [Lawrence] Marrero and what’s the name of the piano player, [Alton] Pernell, his wartime emergency band. Because Bunk was a great trumpet player. And I listened to that band critically, I loved the whole sound. But after a while I realized that, Jim Robinson especially, would play through changes, you know [scats] chord changes. Swinging, nice tone and everything and exciting, but he wasn’t making the changes.…

talk to white people. It was, you know, he came from such a different milieu, you know. I mean it was bad days down there you know. And George once says, isn’t that nice, I’m touched, you know. And so we meet him in the Quarter somewhere and we’re going to go to a funeral. There’s George in a nice suit, Panama hat and a cigarette holder with a cigarette in it. This down home guy, right?
